name: Washed (wet process)
description: The fruit is pulped off and the remaining sticky layer is fermented off in water before drying, leaving just the bare seed to dry.
flavorImpact: Produces the cleanest, brightest cup of the three methods, with acidity and origin character most clearly on display.

name: Natural (dry process)
description: The whole cherry is dried in the sun with the fruit still surrounding the seed, then hulled afterward.
flavorImpact: Produces a fuller-bodied, fruitier, sometimes wine-like or fermented-tasting cup, since the seed absorbs sugars from the drying fruit.

name: Honey process
description: A middle ground — the skin is removed but some or all of the sticky mucilage layer is left on during drying.
flavorImpact: Falls between washed and natural: more body and sweetness than washed, but cleaner and less fruity than natural.
